pages.text: Running beneath the well tree, Taro kicked a coconut shell. Whoosh! All its water spilled into the soil. The quick-handed monkey had been hurrying to play with Mumu.
Sharp-eared deer Mumu turned their ears and bounded over. "I heard a whoosh. What was it?" "Uh... I don't know." Taro quickly turned away.
Mumu looked into the empty shell. "I filled it a moment ago." Taro's heart pounded, and his face felt hot. Ants gathered in lines on the wet soil.
Mumu took the shell to the well. Taro only fiddled with his branch. With no words spoken, the space under the tree was quiet.
Mumu returned with the shell half full and sat beside him. "Taro, I want to play with you." Taro's eyes grew hot.
Taro clenched his hands and breathed out. "I kicked the shell earlier. I'm sorry." Mumu smiled. "I'm Sorry—Now Fill It Again!"
A bucket of water drawn by a grown-up sat on the well's edge. Taro tipped it, filling the shell with gently sloshing water. "I'm Sorry—Now Fill It Again!"
The weight pressing on his chest slipped away. Taro brought the shell in both hands. "Here. Yours first."
Taro patted the wet soil firm. "One, tell right away! Two, say sorry! Three, fill it again!" Mumu took a sip from the tilted shell and nodded.
The ants still lined the wet ground. Mumu gently took Taro's hand. Saying it had made his heart light. Taro lifted the shell. "I'm Sorry—Now Fill It Again!"
